states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released; the new tentative procedure slot is Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival, and that Thursday slot is now specifically a TEE-guided cardioversion case. Scheduler Terry has updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line now says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active.

states.content: Marcus Reed permits use of his cell phone and the patient portal for routine contact, and says the backup line is only for failed reach attempts. His primary contact is his regular cell 617-555-0104, and he asks that any result callbacks use his cell first unless that fails. He asks that the Cedar Bridge number not be called unless his cell fails; the Cedar Bridge front desk stops routing calls after 5 PM, so backup contact through it is limited to daytime. He does not want his cell number used if someone needs to discuss the procedure or his heart rhythm. Backup contact details are not needed unless cardiology requests them. Messages should use generic callback wording only, asking them to have Marcus call Riverside Cardiology back, and must not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing. Routine reminders should go to the patient portal whenever possible. Marcus is fine with the portal wording saying TEE-guided cardioversion, but does not want that wording used in family or voicemail messages.

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Dr. Patel instructs Marcus to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed and not miss any further doses. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Marcus is pretty sure he took his Monday-night apixaban dose, but it was late and he cannot prove the time. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.

states.content: Through Monday, only logistical information may be shared with Nina: arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, and basic transportation instructions. Medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes must not be shared with her. For the tentative Wednesday cardioversion slot, Nina is to be told only the Wednesday time and arrival window, with nothing about the medication plan. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family; family updates should be limited to the logistics scope he set, and nurse Jamison has agreed to keep family updates within that scope. Marcus wants his sister told the times later, but not the reason anything changes. Nurse Elise confirmed that telling Nina the new arrival time without the reason falls within the logistics-only scope through Monday, and she will leave the reason out; she can confirm the updated arrival time only when Marcus permits it and cannot discuss medication adherence or clinical reasons for the schedule change. Marcus explicitly does not want anyone telling Nina that the apixaban dose-timing matter came up. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages.
